identity.class: Group C / IMSA GTP sports prototype
identity.real_world_identity_notes: The submitted XJR-9 maps to Jaguar/Tom Walkinshaw Racing's 1988–1989 Group C and IMSA GTP sports prototype. Exact-car and period sources establish a five-speed dog-leg H-pattern gearbox with no synchronizers, a physical clutch pedal, and a round buttonless steering wheel with analogue instruments. The reviewed sources do not establish integrated rim shift lights or open-top construction.

Jaguar Heritage identifies the original XJR-9, its cockpit, H-pattern gate, lack of synchro, and downshift blip requirement. RM Sotheby's period XJR-9 material gives the exact dogleg five-speed H-pattern gate and clutch description. The repository has no existing exact record.

claims.basis: Jaguar Heritage identifies the original XJR-9, its cockpit, H-pattern gate, lack of synchro, and downshift blip requirement. RM Sotheby's period XJR-9 material gives the exact dogleg five-speed H-pattern gate and clutch description. The repository has no existing exact record.

The exact-model sources describe five forward gears and a five-speed gate. Jaguar Heritage explicitly states that the H-pattern gearshift has no synchro; the project model classifies this non-synchronised racing construction as dogbox. Both exact-model sources describe an H-pattern gearshift/gate. The sources establish three pedals and a progressive physical clutch; an H-pattern gearbox requires clutch control to pull away from rest. The no-synchro dogbox construction supports clutchless running shifts as the authentic technique under the data model; the physical clutch remains available for launch and optional driver use. The no-synchro dogbox construction supports clutchless running downshifts; the source instead explicitly emphasizes accurate shifts and rev matching. Jaguar Heritage directly states that the driver needs to give the XJR-9 a good blip on the way down; this is also consistent with the dogbox derivation. The sourced blip action is specifically a downshift action; no upshift blip is established. No upshift automatic blip action is described. The source prescribes a downshift blip, not a separate downshift lift requirement. No downshift automatic cut procedure is described for the mechanical H-pattern box. Jaguar Heritage directly describes the steering wheel as big and round. The source describes analogue instruments and a buttonless wheel, not an integrated wheel display. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/shift_pattern, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shift_lights, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/open_top.

driver_summary: Dogbox with a dogleg H-pattern: make firm, deliberate shifts and blip every downshift to match revs; the clutch is for launch and is not required for the running shifts. The exact first-gear side of the dogleg remains unconfirmed.
